**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Rule T4C, Termination for convenience**

**What the document says.** §6(a) permits either party to terminate "for any or no reason" on 15 days' notice, but *only* "[a]t any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding." §6(b) covers material breach only. §2 makes the term open-ended, running until terminated under §6.

**Why it fails the fallback.** Once an SOW is live, Clear Capital has no exit route short of Contractor's material breach — and SOWs here are open-ended time-and-materials engagements that can easily run past 12 months. That is the "no Customer right to terminate for convenience" scenario, below the 60–90 day fallback. I did not flag the mutual 15-day right in §6(a): it bites only when no work is outstanding, so RadialSpark cannot abandon a live engagement, and the right benefits us symmetrically (noted in the rationale rather than redlined).

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** New §6(c) after p0033: Company convenience termination of the Agreement or any SOW on 30 days' notice, no termination fee or penalty, payment only for Services performed, refund of prepaid fees, and confirmation that Contractor has no convenience right while an SOW remains uncompleted. Comment offers 60 days' notice as a fallback.
